answer: Someone who burns aliases faster than the churn cap simply runs out of replacements, and the replacements it does make inherit the kernel history. Churn is counted in crystal, and haven publishes the ratio each epoch. At most 23% of an operator's declared identities may be replaced in one epoch, which means rotating keys to dodge slashing does not reset the record. A 98 account operation therefore ties up 26 million dollars of idle capital. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
